submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective, same-position detector of low-content grammatical tokens: it fires strongly on the finite auxiliary 'do' after a subject (' does' active on 63% of its 38 scanned occurrences, ' did' on 59% of 34, ' do' on 18% of 156) and is silent on the infinitive after 'to'/'can'/'will', on 'doing' and 'done' (0/15, 0/31), and on be/have/will/can/could/should/is/was/are/has (all <=3%, with 'have' 9% and 'had' 15% the only weak exceptions); 'the', 'to', 'of', 'with', 'out', 'in' and all possessives except 'his'/'her' stay near zero. Its second component is orthographic rather than syntactic: it fires on the commonest glyph tokens of Greek, Arabic and Bengali ('σι' on 23/23 occurrences, 'τι' 35%, 'ص' 45%, 'ج' 33%, 'ি' 33%) but on none of Chinese ('中' 0/72, '的' 0/345), Cyrillic or accented Latin, and on a scattered set of word-medial fragments of rare words ('hip' in 'spaceship', 'uc' in 'raucous', 'itting' in 'unfitting', 'ru' in 'Thruway', 'ight' in 'Speight') even though most multi-token words ('delimiter', 'conqueror', 'atonement', 'government') are silent; capitalisation, proper-noun identity, surprisal, entropy, token frequency and part of speech do not predict it.

Oftentimes, I hear a person in my office say, “I shouldn’t feel that way,” I don’t like that I have these bad feelings.”
They are down on themselves because they have a “bad” feeling. There is no such thing as a “bad” feeling and, therefore, no basis to feel guilty about having one. Let me elaborate.
Let’s start with this. Do you know the difference between emotions and feelings? There is one. They are two sides of the same coin and highly interconnected, but are two different things. Debbie Hampton has written an elucidating article about this, based on the wisdom of a few noted neuroscientists.
EMOTIONS are lower level responses occurring in the subcortical regions of the brain, the amygdale and the ventromedial cortices, creating biochemical reactions in your body altering your physical state. Emotional reactions are coded in our genes.
FEELINGS: “Feelings originate in the neocortical regions of the brain, are mental associations and reactions to emotions, and are subjective, being influenced by personal experience, beliefs, and memories. A feeling is a mental portrayal of what is going on in your body when you have an emotion and is the byproduct of your brain perceiving and assigning meaning to the emotion. Feelings are the next thing that happens after having an emotion, involving cognitive input, usually subconscious, and cannot be measured precisely.”
Dr. Antonio D’Amasio, neuroscientist professor at the University of California, states it this way: “Feelings are mental experiences of body states, which arise as the brain interprets emotions, themselves physical states arising from the body’s response to external stimuli. (The order of events is: I am threatened, experience fear (emotion) and feel horror).”
While basic emotions are instinctual and common to us all, the meanings they take on and the feelings they prompt are individual based on your programming past and present. Feelings are shaped by a person’s temperament and experiences and vary greatly from person to person and situation to situation.
Whew! You’re probably saying, “TMI” (Too Much Information)! The reason I share this information is I believe so strongly in the brain wiring process and I want you to understand it and take an active role in the continuing shaping of your brain, through the reality of neuroplasticity. It is important to know how you are brain wired so that you can understand what emotions and feelings that you have. Understanding this, you can make more enlightened choices as to the behavior you choose after these emotional and feeling states arise in your mind and body.
Bottom line here, and the basis for the headline of this article, is that emotions and feelings just happen. They are instinctual reflexes. You do not choose them. So quit feeling bad (a cognitive choice) about having a nasty feeling.
Let me use an example: Someone hurts someone you love. The EMOTION of anger arises. The FEELING of hate for that person comes next. Then the cognitive THOUGH

I think owning an Arcade Machine was always one of my top wishes in the never ending want-to-have list when I was younger. The Arcade feeling is probably something which got lost with the Playstation Generation of gamers but I can connect a lot of memories with Arcades.
So sometimes last year I was thinking about building a MAME cabinet myself. I searched for some viable information on the web to look for good pointers. Some people build their cabinet from scratch, some use existing ones and remove all the original hardware but the Monitor and Sticks. Some looked horrible, some awesome.
As I am actually not a good carpenter I went with the plan to buy an existing machine to convert it to a MAME Cabinet. But then the next questions came up. What cabinet should I buy? What does it take to convert it to MAME. All I wanted is a cab which looked okay, worked well and was easy to mod.
Coincidentally some guy in one of the videogame forums I visit daily sold a Sega New Net City cab. It had the perfect foundation. It had a modern look, one of the best monitors from an arcade standpoint and lots of space inside, enough to hide a nice PC and all cables I had to add for the MAME experience. The monitor already came with standard VGA Outputs and the cabinet board had chinch connectors for the audio - it was perfect!
I then bought a silent HTPC with some good specs and it fitted nicely into the available space. Two XBOX360 Pads were disassembled and wired to the original arcade controls. The PC would recognize them via USB and I was able to map the sticks and 14 buttons without hassle in the MAME frontend.
Speaking of Frontends, I experimented with Hyperspin but to be honest , all I wanted was to quickly play a game and not put 1+TB on Videofiles on my machine. So I ended up using MAMEUIFX - a simple straight forward MAME Frontend. To control it I connected a wireless Keyboard. You turn the cabinet on and can play within seconds. All I do i hit STRG-F to find a game in question and hit return and there we go.
What can I say - it's perfect, really. I am also glad my son can experience this too. We are a couple of times per week downstairs to play games like Bubble Bobble or Thunder Cross - he likes it.
Below are some pictures from the in- and outside plus some bonus photos of the pain getting this thing down to the basement and unpacked. If you have not grown up with large CRT Monitors you probably can not even imagine how heavy that stuff is - I had backache for a week - but it was worth it.

Friday, 13 June 2008

An elderly former teacher who sexually abused three young boys will not be eligible for release from jail for at least six years.

Ronald Lewis Tuckwell, 74, has been sentenced to 10 years' jail by the District Court in Adelaide.

He pleaded guilty to nine charges of unlawful sexual intercourse and indecent assault.

The first offence in 1959 involved a 11-year-old boy and the others occurred in the late 1970s and early 1980s, also involving young boys.

Outside the court, the sentence has been welcomed by one of the victims.

"Surprised, but happy, and again I would say I feel it is just," he said.

Chief Judge Terry Worthington said the crimes were callous and involved a gross breach of trust against vulnerable and defenceless children.

ια ξύλινη βαλβίδα. Εκεί, πρέπει να εκτελέσουν το άλμα. Η απόσταση από την άκρη της βαλβίδας, μέχρι το κοντινότερο βαθούλωμα στο σκάμμα, αποτελεί την επίδοση του αθλητή στην συγκεκριμένη προσπάθεια. Αν ο αθλητής πατήσει πέρα από την βαλβίδα, η προσπάθεια ακυρώνεται και η απόσταση δεν προσμετράται. Το αγώνισμα θα διεξαχθεί σε 2 γύρους: Έναν προκριματικό και τον τελικό.

Το αγώνισμα θα πραγματοποιηθεί σε δύο γύρους: Έναν προκριματικό και τον τελικό. Στον προκριματικό γύρο, κάθε αθλητής έχει στη διάθεσή του 3 άλματα στα οποία πρέπει να ξεπεράσει τα 8,15 μέτρα, που αποτελούν όριο πρόκρισης για τον τελικό, στον οποίο υπάρχουν 12 διαθέσιμες θέσεις. Αν λιγότεροι από 12 άλτες ξεπεράσουν το όριο, οι διαθέσιμες θέσεις δίνονται στους αθλητές με τις επόμενες καλύτερες επιδόσεις. Στον τελικό, κάθε άλτης έχει πάλι στην διάθεσή του 3 άλματα. Οι 8 άλτες με την καλύτερη επίδοση, κερδίζουν ακόμα 3 άλματα (σύνολο 6), προκειμένω να βελτιώσουν την επίδοσή τους. Στο τέλος του αγώνα, από τις 6 προσπάθειες μετράει η καλύτερη του κάθε αθλητή και νικητής είναι αυτός με το μεγαλύτερο άλμα.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Three does grazed along the meadow edge while the buck watched from the treeline.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'does' here is the plural noun for female deer, not the finite auxiliary, so the hypothesis predicts silence despite the same token after a determiner.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They booked the village hall for the school's end-of-term do and invited every parent.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Nominal 'do' (a party) preceded by a possessive; the same surface token in a non-verbal role, which the hypothesis excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The choir sang do re mi fa sol before running the anthem twice.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Solfège 'do', a musical syllable rather than a verb, so the auxiliary-only account predicts no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Marta does the dishes every evening while Tomas dries them.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lexical main-verb 'does' with a direct object: it is finite and follows a subject, but it is not the auxiliary role the hypothesis names, so it should stay silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He did the crossword in ten minutes and then folded the paper away.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lexical main-verb 'did' taking a direct object rather than do-support; the hypothesis's finite-auxiliary role is absent, so it predicts silence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The boy was doing homework at the kitchen table when the lights flickered.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis states 'doing' is silent (0/15 scanned occurrences).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We have done enough for one night, so put the tools back in the shed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'done' is explicitly silent (0/31) and 'have' is at most a weak exception in the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I want to do the whole thing properly before the deadline on Friday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Infinitive 'do' after 'to', which the hypothesis explicitly says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She can do better than that if she takes time and checks the figures.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Infinitive 'do' after modal 'can', one of the silent environments the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They will do whatever the supervisor asks, provided the order arrives.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Infinitive 'do' after 'will', another explicitly silent environment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She kept asking: does the committee meet on Fridays, or only when a quorum exists?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Subject-auxiliary inversion: 'does' precedes its subject, so under the hypothesis's 'after a subject' condition it should stay silent even though it is a finite auxiliary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 在过去几十年中，中国的经济取得了显著的成就。
adversarial_test_results.detail: '中' and '的' are the hypothesis's explicit zero cases in Chinese (0/72 and 0/345), and the token check confirms both appear as standalone tokens; predicted silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Государственная дума приняла закон в первом чтении, и президент подписал его.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cyrillic text, which the hypothesis says the orthographic component never fires on.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: La réforme agraire a été adoptée après des années de débat à l'Assemblée.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Accented Latin script, which the hypothesis states does not fire, though the sentence is dense with low-content grammatical words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The delimiter is set in the configuration file, and the conqueror metaphor appears only in the preface.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis names 'delimiter' and 'conqueror' as multi-token words that remain silent; the check confirms they split into ' delim'+'iter' and ' conquer'+'or'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cat wandered out of the kitchen and sat in with the guests by the fire.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Packed with 'out', 'of', 'the', 'in', 'with', the function words the hypothesis places near zero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Their report arrived late, and its conclusions contradicted the earlier draft.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'Their' and 'its' are possessives, which the hypothesis says stay near zero apart from 'his' and 'her'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: تحدث الوزير عن خطة للتعليم في المدارس الريفية.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Arabic lacking 'ص' and 'ج', the only Arabic glyph tokens the hypothesis claims can fire; the token check confirms neither appears.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: আমরা এখন স্কুলে যাব এবং সন্ধ্যা পর্যন্ত সেখানে থাকব।
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bengali with no 'ি' vowel sign, the only Bengali token the hypothesis claims fires; predicted silent.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Η έκθεση αναφέρει πως η οικονομία αναπτύσσεται με αργούς ρυθμούς φέτος.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Greek containing neither 'σι' nor 'τι', the two Greek glyph tokens the hypothesis claims can fire; the token check confirms the split yields 'σ'+'σε'+'ται'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Recent evidence suggests that the protein does not fold correctly under mild heat, which may account for the earlier failures.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Finite auxiliary 'does' after a non-pronoun subject in scientific prose, a genre absent from the examples; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Margaret did not answer at once; she set the teacup down and stared past him at the door.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Finite auxiliary 'did' after a proper-noun subject in narrative dialogue; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: These sensors do not need calibration, and they report every reading to the base station each night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Finite auxiliary 'do' after a plural noun subject, where the examples only showed 'I do'; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When the interviewer asked whether I still painted, I said that I do, though not as often now.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Elliptical finite 'do' with no following verb but still after its subject; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Η χρησιμοποίηση των δημόσιων πόρων κρίθηκε σωστή από την επιτροπή.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New Greek word 'χρησιμοποίηση' carrying the glyph 'σι' as its own token (twice in the sentence), which the hypothesis says fires on 23/23 of its occurrences.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: أصدرت الوزارة قرارا جديدا بشأن المصارف بعد أشهر من الجدل.
adversarial_test_results.detail: New Arabic sentence containing 'ص' and 'ج', the glyph tokens the hypothesis says can fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের শিক্ষার্থীরা নতুন পাঠক্রম শুরু করেছে এই সপ্তাহে।
adversarial_test_results.detail: New Bengali sentence containing the 'ি' vowel sign as a standalone token, predicted active by the orthographic component.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The apprenticeship at the foundry ended when the works finally closed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'hip' survives as its own token inside 'apprenticeship', the word-medial fragment pattern the hypothesis claims ('hip' in 'spaceship'); predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The yard spent the winter refitting the trawler and outfitting it with new winches.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'itting' survives as its own token inside 'refitting', matching the claimed 'itting' fragment ('unfitting'); predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She found his notebook under the bed and her scarf behind the radiator.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Possessives 'his' and 'her', which the hypothesis singles out as firing while other possessives do not.
